questions.q: Select the antonym of the word 'Censure'.
questions.x: 'Censure' is the opposite of 'Praise'. The other options are similar in meaning to 'Censure'.

questions.q: Select the synonym of the word 'Venerate'.
questions.x: 'Venerate' means revere. 'Despise' is close to its opposite; the others are unrelated or look-alike words.

questions.q:
Identify the segment of the sentence that contains a grammatical error. If the sentence is correct, choose 'No error'.
Bread and butter / is / his usual breakfast.
questions.x: The sentence is grammatically correct as written. Correct: 'bread and butter' is treated as a single item.

questions.q: Choose the word OPPOSITE in meaning to: CONCUR
questions.x: 'Concur' is the opposite of 'Disagree'. The other options are similar in meaning to 'Concur'.

questions.q: Choose the option that best expresses the meaning of the idiom: 'To be up in arms'
o: To be very angry and protesting
questions.x: 'To be up in arms' means: to be very angry and protesting.

questions.q: What does the phrase 'To take with a pinch of salt' mean?
o: To be very careful with money
questions.x: 'To take with a pinch of salt' means: to regard with scepticism.

questions.q: The new policy will ____ effect from the first of next month.
questions.x: 'Come into effect' means to begin to apply.

questions.q: Select the synonym of the word 'Ephemeral'.
questions.x: 'Ephemeral' means short-lived. 'Eternal' is close to its opposite; the others are unrelated or look-alike words.

questions.q: Select the antonym of the word 'Futile'.
questions.x: 'Futile' is the opposite of 'Fruitful'. The other options are similar in meaning to 'Futile'.

questions.q: Choose the word that is most nearly SAME in meaning to: UBIQUITOUS
questions.x: 'Ubiquitous' means omnipresent. 'Rare' is close to its opposite; the others are unrelated or look-alike words.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT mentioned as a service provided by forests?
questions.x: Answer: 'Generating electricity'. Electricity generation is not mentioned. The other options either add ideas not found in the passage or contradict it.
questions.p: Forests are often valued only for timber, but their greater worth lies in services we rarely price: holding soil, recharging springs, storing carbon and sheltering wildlife. When a hillside is cleared, these services disappear quietly until floods or landslides reveal the loss. Paying communities to protect forests recognises that the people living nearest to them are their most effective guardians.

questions.q: The phrase 'disappear quietly' suggests that the loss of forest services:
o: Goes unnoticed until a disaster reveals it
questions.x: Answer: 'Goes unnoticed until a disaster reveals it'. The passage says the loss is revealed by floods or landslides. The other options either add ideas not found in the passage or contradict it.
questions.p: Forests are often valued only for timber, but their greater worth lies in services we rarely price: holding soil, recharging springs, storing carbon and sheltering wildlife. When a hillside is cleared, these services disappear quietly until floods or landslides reveal the loss. Paying communities to protect forests recognises that the people living nearest to them are their most effective guardians.

questions.q: The Alipore Bomb Case (1908) is associated with:
questions.x: Correct answer: Aurobindo Ghosh and Barindra Ghosh. Aurobindo was acquitted, defended by C. R. Das.

questions.q: Choose the correct year for this event: the Moplah (Mappila) rebellion broke out in Malabar.
questions.x: The Moplah (Mappila) rebellion broke out in Malabar in 1921. Fix this date on your 1857–1947 timeline along with the events immediately before and after it.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): The Communal Award (1932) was opposed by Gandhi.
Reason (R): It provided separate electorates for the depressed classes.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: A is true and R is true; R correctly explains A. Gandhi fasted in Yerawada jail against separate electorates for depressed classes, leading to the Poona Pact.

questions.q: Who presided over the 1919 session of the Indian National Congress held at Amritsar?
questions.x: Motilal Nehru presided over the 1919 Amritsar session — the session held after the Jallianwala Bagh massacre.

questions.q: After 1857, the 'Queen's Proclamation' of 1858 was read out at:
questions.x: It transferred power from the East India Company to the Crown and promised non-interference in religion.

questions.q: V. R. Shinde is associated with the founding of:
questions.x: V. R. Shinde founded the Depressed Classes Mission (1906).

questions.q: The 'Kheda Satyagraha' of 1918 was about:
o: Remission of land revenue after crop failure
questions.x: Correct answer: Remission of land revenue after crop failure. Vallabhbhai Patel emerged as a leader in this struggle.

questions.q: 'Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it' was the declaration of:
questions.x: Correct answer: Bal Gangadhar Tilak. Tilak popularised Ganapati and Shivaji festivals to mobilise people.

questions.q: The 'Forest Satyagraha' in the 1930s was prominent in which region?
questions.x: Correct answer: Central Provinces, Maharashtra and Karnataka. Forest laws were defied during Civil Disobedience.

questions.q: The 'Pabna revolt' (1873) was:
o: An agrarian league of tenants against zamindars' high rents in East Bengal
questions.x: Correct answer: An agrarian league of tenants against zamindars' high rents in East Bengal. Peasants formed agrarian leagues and fought legally.

questions.q: National Voters' Day is observed on:
questions.x: National Voters' Day: 25 January.

questions.q: Keir Starmer became the Prime Minister of the United Kingdom in July 2024, leading which party?
questions.x: Correct answer: Labour Party. He succeeded Rishi Sunak.

questions.q: The 2025 Nobel Prize in Physics was awarded for the discovery of:
o: Macroscopic quantum tunnelling and energy quantisation in an electric circuit
questions.x: Correct answer: Macroscopic quantum tunnelling and energy quantisation in an electric circuit. John Clarke, Michel Devoret and John Martinis were the laureates.

questions.q: The military exercise 'Garuda Shakti' is conducted between India and:
questions.x: 'Garuda Shakti' is a bilateral exercise between India and Indonesia.

questions.q: The 'International Big Cat Alliance', launched by India in 2023, covers how many big cat species?
questions.x: Correct answer: Seven. Tiger, lion, leopard, snow leopard, cheetah, jaguar and puma.

questions.q: 'Operation Kaveri' (2023) was the evacuation of Indians from:
questions.x: Correct answer: Sudan. Indian Air Force and Navy assets were used.

questions.q: Which of the following organisations is headquartered in Rome?
questions.x: International Fund for Agricultural Development is based in Rome.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the WHO Pandemic Agreement (2025):
1. It was adopted by the World Health Assembly.
2. It includes a Pathogen Access and Benefit-Sharing (PABS) system to be detailed in an annex.
3. The United States led the negotiations to completion.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
The US had announced withdrawal from the WHO and did not take part in its adoption.

questions.q: Which site was inscribed as India's 43rd UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2024?
o: Moidams — mound-burial system of the Ahom dynasty, Charaideo
questions.x: Santiniketan and the Hoysala temples were inscribed in 2023; Dholavira in 2021.

questions.q: The 'State of Food Security and Nutrition in the World' is published by:
o: FAO with IFAD, UNICEF, WFP and WHO
questions.x: 'State of Food Security and Nutrition in the World' is brought out by FAO with IFAD, UNICEF, WFP and WHO.

questions.q: Which Article of the Constitution of India provides for: "Administrative Tribunals"?
questions.x: This subject is dealt with in Article 323A.

questions.q: The constitutional amendment that incorporated Goa, Daman and Diu into the Indian Union was enacted in the year:
questions.x: This was the 12th Amendment Act, 1962.

questions.q: The 'Objectives Resolution' and the Preamble were adopted with which date chosen for the Constitution's commencement in honour of the 1930 'Purna Swaraj' declaration?
questions.x: 26 January 1930 was celebrated as Purna Swaraj Day; hence the Constitution commenced on 26 January 1950.

questions.q: Untouchability is an offence punishable under the:
questions.x: Correct answer: Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955. Originally the Untouchability (Offences) Act, 1955, renamed in 1976.

questions.q: Article 74 of the Constitution of India deals with:
o: State Election Commission for elections to Panchayats
Council of Ministers to aid and advise the President
Sessions of Parliament, prorogation and dissolution
questions.x: Article 74: Council of Ministers to aid and advise the President.

questions.q: Which motion is moved to draw the attention of a minister to a matter of urgent public importance?
questions.x: Correct answer: Calling attention motion. It is an Indian innovation in parliamentary procedure since 1954.

questions.q: Which writ can be issued against a public authority as well as a private individual?
questions.x: Habeas corpus lies against any person or authority detaining someone unlawfully.

questions.q: Which Article provides for the official language of a State?
questions.x: Correct answer: Article 345. Article 351 directs the Union to promote the spread of Hindi.

questions.q: A Legislative Council in a State can be created or abolished by Parliament if the State Assembly passes a resolution by:
o: A majority of its total membership and two-thirds of members present and voting
questions.x: Article 169; such a law is not deemed a constitutional amendment under Article 368.

questions.q: The Central Vigilance Commission got statutory status through the:
questions.x: The CVC was set up in 1964 on the Santhanam Committee's recommendation and given statutory status in 2003.

questions.q: 'Priority sector lending' requires domestic commercial banks to lend at least what share of Adjusted Net Bank Credit to priority sectors?
questions.x: Sub-targets include 18% for agriculture and 7.5% for micro enterprises.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): Indirect taxes are generally regressive.
Reason (R): Indirect taxes are levied at the same rate on everyone regardless of income.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: A is true and R is true; R correctly explains A. Because the rate is the same, lower-income people pay a higher share of their income.

questions.q: The Abid Hussain Committee (1997) is associated with:
o: Economic capital framework of the RBI
questions.x: Abid Hussain Committee (1997): Small-scale industries.

questions.q: In a simple banking model, the cash reserve ratio is 4% and banks keep no excess reserves. A fresh deposit of ₹1400 crore can lead to a maximum total deposit creation of:
questions.x:
Deposit (money) multiplier = 1 / CRR = 1 / 0.04 = 25.
Total deposits = 1400 × 25 = ₹35,000 crore (of which new credit = ₹33,600 crore).

questions.q: The 'Fair and Remunerative Price' is announced for:
questions.x: Correct answer: Sugarcane. It replaced the Statutory Minimum Price in 2009.

questions.q: Transfer payments such as old-age pensions are excluded from national income because:
o: They are not payments for current productive services
questions.x: Correct answer: They are not payments for current productive services. Including them would amount to double counting.

questions.q: Who among the following benefits from unanticipated inflation?
questions.x: Correct answer: Borrowers with fixed nominal interest. Inflation erodes the real value of debt.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): Inflation hurts people with fixed incomes.
Reason (R): Inflation reduces the purchasing power of money.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: A is true and R is true; R correctly explains A. Fixed incomes buy less as prices rise.

questions.q: The Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act was enacted — in which year?
questions.x: The Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act was enacted in 2003.

questions.q: The India–EFTA Trade and Economic Partnership Agreement (signed 2024) is notable for:
o: A commitment by EFTA countries to promote investment of US$ 100 billion in India over 15 years
questions.x: EFTA comprises Switzerland, Norway, Iceland and Liechtenstein; the agreement entered into force in October 2025.

questions.q: A partner withdrew ₹5,500 at the middle of every month during the year. Interest on drawings is charged at 6% p.a. The interest on drawings is:
questions.x:
Total drawings = 12 × 5,500 = ₹66,000.
Average period for monthly drawings made at the middle of each month = 6 months.
Interest = 66,000 × 6% × 6/12 = ₹1,980.

questions.q: From the following, compute Gross Profit: Opening stock ₹30,000; Purchases ₹3,15,000; Purchase returns ₹4,000; Carriage inwards ₹2,000; Sales ₹3,63,000; Sales returns ₹4,000; Closing stock ₹25,000.
questions.x:
Cost of goods sold = Opening stock + Purchases − Purchase returns + Carriage inwards − Closing stock
= 30,000 + 3,15,000 − 4,000 + 2,000 − 25,000 = ₹3,18,000.
Gross profit = Net sales − COGS = 3,63,000 − 4,000 − 3,18,000 = ₹41,000.
Carriage inwards is a direct expense (Trading A/c).

questions.q: A 'right issue' of shares means shares offered to:
o: Existing shareholders in proportion to their holdings
questions.x: Correct answer: Existing shareholders in proportion to their holdings. Section 62 provides for rights issues.

questions.q: Debtors (trade receivables) turnover ratio is computed as:
o: Net credit sales ÷ Average trade receivables
questions.x: Correct answer: Net credit sales ÷ Average trade receivables. Average collection period = 365 ÷ debtors turnover.

questions.q: Goods sent on 'sale or return' basis and not yet approved by the customer at the year-end should be:
o: Included in closing stock at cost, and the sale reversed
questions.x: The sale is not complete until approval; goods remain the seller's stock.

questions.q: Purchase of machinery for ₹40,000 was debited to Purchases account. The rectification entry is:
o: Machinery A/c Dr. To Suspense A/c ₹40,000
Suspense A/c Dr. To Purchases A/c ₹40,000
Purchases A/c Dr. To Machinery A/c ₹40,000
Machinery A/c Dr. To Purchases A/c ₹40,000
questions.x: Correct answer: Machinery A/c Dr. To Purchases A/c ₹40,000. An error of principle; no suspense account is involved.

questions.q: In the indirect method of computing cash from operating activities, depreciation is:
questions.x: Correct answer: Added back to net profit. Depreciation is a non-cash expense.

questions.q: Under Section 143(12) of the Companies Act, 2013, an auditor who has reason to believe that a fraud involving ₹1 crore or more is being committed must report to:
questions.x: Correct answer: The Central Government. Frauds below the threshold are reported to the audit committee/board.

questions.q: Machinery costing ₹2,30,000 is depreciated at 10% per annum on the Written Down Value method. Its book value at the end of 3 years will be:
questions.x:
WDV: depreciation each year is charged on the opening book value.
Book value = Cost × (1 − r)ⁿ = 2,30,000 × (0.9)^3 = ₹1,67,670.
(SLM at the same rate would give ₹1,61,000.)

questions.q: The cash book of a firm shows a debit (bank) balance of ₹39,000. Cheques issued but not yet presented: ₹2,500; cheques deposited but not yet credited: ₹1,000; bank charges debited only in the pass book: ₹350; interest credited only in the pass book: ₹700. The balance as per the pass book is:
questions.x:
Start with cash book balance ₹39,000.
+ Cheques issued not presented (bank has not yet paid) 2,500
− Cheques deposited not credited 1,000
− Bank charges 350
+ Interest credited 700
Pass book balance = ₹40,850.

questions.q: Office furniture is purchased for ₹3,30,000 and ₹2,000 is spent on its installation. Its estimated useful life is 4 years with a residual value of ₹4,000. Annual depreciation under the Straight Line Method is:
questions.x:
SLM depreciation = (Cost + installation − residual value) / useful life.
= (3,30,000 + 2,000 − 4,000) / 4 = 3,28,000 / 4 = ₹82,000 per year.
Installation is capitalised as part of cost (AS 10 / Ind AS 16).

questions.q: Fixed costs are ₹72,000; selling price ₹120 and variable cost ₹100 per unit. How many units must be sold to earn a profit of ₹40,000?
questions.x:
Required units = (Fixed cost + Target profit) / Contribution per unit
= (72,000 + 40,000) / 20 = 5,600 units.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): A trial balance that agrees proves that the books are free from all errors.
Reason (R): Errors of principle and compensating errors do not affect the agreement of a trial balance.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: A is false but R is true. A is false (agreement does not prove absence of errors). R is true and actually shows why A is false.

questions.q: P and Q share profits in the ratio 5 : 4. They admit R for a 1/5 share, which R acquires from P and Q in their existing ratio. The new profit-sharing ratio of P, Q and R is:
Under the Code on Wages, if excluded components such as HRA, conveyance and overtime exceed a certain share of total remuneration, the excess is added back to 'wages'. That share is:
questions.x: The proviso to Section 2(y) deems the amount by which excluded payments exceed one-half (50%) of total remuneration to be wages — this prevents a deflated 'basic' for computing PF, gratuity etc.

questions.q: Which judgment held that a domestic inquiry is not required if the employer proves misconduct before the Tribunal, which can then decide on the punishment?
o: Indian Iron & Steel Co. v. Workmen (1958)
State of Punjab v. Mohinder Singh (1997)
Workmen of Firestone Tyre & Rubber Co. v. Management (1973)
questions.x: Firestone Tyre (1973) summarised principles on domestic inquiry and explained Section 11A powers.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT 'retrenchment' as defined in Indian labour law?
o: Termination following closure of a department
Termination due to introduction of new machinery
Termination as a punishment inflicted by way of disciplinary action
questions.x: Retrenchment excludes disciplinary punishment, voluntary retirement, superannuation, non-renewal of fixed-term contract and termination on continued ill-health.

questions.q: Walton and McKersie's 'behavioural theory of labour negotiations' (1965) identified four sub-processes. Which of these is one of them?
questions.x: The four sub-processes are distributive bargaining, integrative bargaining, attitudinal structuring and intra-organisational bargaining.

questions.q: Under the Trade Unions Act, 1926 (now in the IR Code), the 'general fund' of a registered union could be spent on certain objects; political objects had to be met from:
o: A separate political fund with voluntary contributions
questions.x: A separate fund for political purposes, contributed voluntarily, was required; members could not be compelled to contribute.

questions.q: In which year was the Industrial Employment (Standing Orders) Act enacted?
questions.x: The Industrial Employment (Standing Orders) Act was enacted in 1946.

questions.q: The definition of inter-State migrant worker in the OSH Code covers a worker earning up to (or as notified):
questions.x: An inter-State migrant worker is one who comes from another State and draws wages up to ₹18,000 per month (or as notified).

questions.q: Which of these laws continues to operate outside the four Labour Codes?
o: Child and Adolescent Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act, 1986
questions.x: The child labour law was not codified. Standing Orders went into the IR Code, Motor Transport Workers into the OSH Code and Payment of Wages into the Code on Wages.

questions.q: ILO Convention No. 144 (1976), which India has ratified, relates to:
o: Tripartite consultation on international labour standards
questions.x: C144 requires tripartite consultations on ILO matters; it is a governance (priority) convention.

questions.q: Under the Maternity Benefit Act, how many days of work in the twelve months preceding the expected delivery are required for eligibility?
questions.x: A woman must have actually worked for at least 80 days in the 12 months immediately preceding her expected delivery date.

questions.q: Who is the 'appropriate government' for an establishment in the central public sector under the IR Code?
o: Central Government (for CPSUs in which Centre holds 50% or more of the share capital)
questions.x: For a central public sector undertaking or a company in which the Centre holds at least 50% equity, the Central Government is the appropriate government.

questions.q: Under the IR Code, office-bearers of a registered trade union in the organised sector who are not actually engaged in the establishment can be at most:
o: One-third of the office-bearers or five, whichever is less
questions.x: Outsiders are limited to one-third or five, whichever is less; in the unorganised sector up to half may be outsiders.

questions.q: Workers of a mill give a strike notice on 1 March. Under the IR Code, the strike can lawfully begin:
o: On or after 15 March but within 60 days of the notice, if no conciliation is pending
questions.x: The strike cannot take place within 14 days of notice and must take place within 60 days; conciliation pendency also bars strikes.

questions.q: A significant change in the IR Code regarding strike notice is that it now applies to:
o: All industrial establishments, not just public utility services
questions.x: Under the ID Act notice was mandatory only in public utility services; the IR Code extends the notice requirement to all industrial establishments.

questions.q: If a region has a population of 1,000, a labour force of 550 and 517 employed persons, its LFPR and unemployment rate are respectively:
Under the Code on Social Security, the Social Security Fund for unorganised, gig and platform workers is to be administered by:
o: The Central Government, with the National Social Security Board advising on schemes
questions.x: The Fund is set up by the Central Government; the National Social Security Board recommends and monitors schemes for these workers.

questions.q: A woman employee entitled to 12 weeks of maternity benefit has an average daily wage of ₹530. Following the Supreme Court's view in B. Shah v. Presiding Officer (1977) that the benefit covers all days of the period, the total maternity benefit is:
questions.x:
The benefit is paid for every day of the 12-week period including Sundays: 12 × 7 = 84 days.
Amount = ₹530 × 84 = ₹44,520. (Using 6 days/week would wrongly give ₹38,160.)

questions.q: Under a June 2025 decision, the limit for auto-settlement of EPF advance claims without manual intervention was raised to:
questions.x: Auto-settlement for advance claims (illness, education, marriage, housing) was raised from ₹1 lakh to ₹5 lakh.

questions.q: An EPS member opts for early pension at 56, with a full pension (at 58) entitlement of ₹5,000. The early pension will be about:
questions.x: Reduction of 4% per year short of 58: 2 years → 8%; ₹5,000 × 0.92 = ₹4,600.

questions.q: The Central Government Health Scheme (CGHS) primarily serves:
questions.x: CGHS provides health care to central government employees, pensioners and dependants in notified cities.

questions.q: Antyodaya Anna Yojana (AAY) households under NFSA are entitled to how much foodgrain per month?
questions.x: AAY households, the poorest of the poor, get 35 kg per household per month.

questions.q: Under the Code on Social Security, registration of unorganised, gig and platform workers is based on:
o: Self-declaration with Aadhaar on a portal
questions.x: Workers self-register using Aadhaar (e-Shram), receiving a unique number.

questions.q: An insured employee earns gross wages of ₹15,500 in a month. What is the total ESI contribution (employer + employee) payable for that month?
questions.x:
Employee share 0.75% = ₹116.25 → ₹117; employer share 3.25% = ₹503.75 → ₹504 (rounded up to the next rupee).
Total = ₹621 (4% of wages; rates in force since 1 July 2019).

questions.q: Under the Unified Pension Scheme, family pension on the death of the pensioner is:
questions.x: The spouse receives 60% of the pension admissible immediately before death.

questions.q: EPF administrative charges payable by employers since June 2018 are:
o: 0.50% of EPF wages, subject to a monthly minimum
questions.x: Administrative charges were reduced to 0.50% from June 2018 (from 0.65%); EDLI administrative charges were abolished from April 2017.

questions.q: The 'Beveridgean' model of social security emphasises:
o: Universal coverage with flat-rate benefits, largely tax-financed
questions.x: Correct answer: Universal coverage with flat-rate benefits, largely tax-financed. Beveridge's plan aimed at a national minimum for all citizens.

questions.q:
Match the scheme with its launch year:
Scheme:
A. EDLI
B. EPS
C. NPS (government employees)
D. APY
Year:
1. 2004
2. 2015
3. 1976
4. 1995
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.x:
Correct matching — A (EDLI) → 3 (1976); B (EPS) → 4 (1995); C (NPS (government employees)) → 1 (2004); D (APY) → 2 (2015).
EDLI 1976, EPS 1995, NPS 2004, APY 2015.

questions.q: To be eligible for sickness benefit under ESI, contributions should have been paid for at least how many days in the corresponding contribution period?
questions.x: The insured person must have contributed for at least 78 days in the six-month contribution period.

questions.q: An object appears black when it:
o: Absorbs all wavelengths of visible light
questions.x: Correct answer: Absorbs all wavelengths of visible light. A white object reflects all wavelengths.

questions.q: The national helpline number for reporting cyber financial fraud in India is:
questions.x: Correct answer: 1930. Complaints can also be filed on cybercrime.gov.in.

questions.q: The causative agent of filariasis is:
o: Wuchereria bancrofti (nematode worm, spread by Culex mosquitoes)
Dengue virus (a flavivirus spread by Aedes mosquitoes)
questions.x: Filariasis: Wuchereria bancrofti (nematode worm, spread by Culex mosquitoes).

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Insulin — Pancreas
2. Thyroxine — Thyroid
3. Adrenaline — Adrenal gland
4. Growth hormone — Pituitary
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.x:
4 of the 4 listed items satisfy the condition asked.
All four pairs are correctly matched.

questions.q: The energy of the Sun is produced mainly by:
questions.x: Correct answer: Fusion of hydrogen into helium. Fusion releases enormous energy.

questions.q: Which blood group is called the 'universal donor'?
questions.x: Correct answer: O negative. AB positive is the universal recipient.

questions.q: A 'search engine' is:
o: A program that searches the web for information based on keywords
questions.x: Correct answer: A program that searches the web for information based on keywords. Google, Bing and DuckDuckGo are examples.

questions.q: The number of bones in an adult human body is:
questions.x: Correct answer: 206. Newborns have about 300 bones, many of which fuse.

questions.q: The hardest natural substance is:
questions.x: Diamond and graphite are allotropes of carbon; graphite is soft and conducts electricity.

questions.q: Which abbreviation stands for 'Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol'?
questions.x: Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol is abbreviated as DHCP.

questions.q: Leguminous plants enrich soil with nitrogen because their root nodules contain:
questions.x: Correct answer: Rhizobium bacteria. Rhizobium fixes atmospheric nitrogen.

questions.q: In computing, 'latency' refers to:
o: The delay before data transfer begins following an instruction
questions.x: Correct answer: The delay before data transfer begins following an instruction. Low latency is important for gaming and video calls.

questions.q: Find the odd one out among 26, 1331, 512 and 27.
questions.x: 27, 512, 1331 are all perfect cubes; 26 is not. Hence 26 is the odd one out.

questions.q: In a row, Rahul is 19th from the left and Tanya is 16th from the right. When they interchange their positions, Rahul becomes 28th from the left. How many persons are there in the row?
questions.x:
After interchange, Rahul occupies Tanya's old place, which is 16th from the right and now 28th from the left.
Total = 28 + 16 − 1 = 43.

questions.q: What is the remainder when 917 × 932 × 830 is divided by 7?
questions.x:
Use remainders: 917 mod 7 = 0, 932 mod 7 = 1, 830 mod 7 = 4.
0 × 1 × 4 = 0 → mod 7 = 0.

questions.q: Find the next term of the series: 67, 84, 103, 124, 147, ?
questions.x: Terms are 8²+3, 9²+3, … so the next is 13² + 3 = 172.

questions.q: On which day of the week did 16 December 1863 fall?
questions.x:
Odd-day method (Sunday = 0).
Completed years = 1862: 1600 years → 0 odd days; 200 years → 3; remaining 62 years have 15 leap + 47 ordinary → 15×2 + 47 = 77 → 0 odd day(s).
Days elapsed in 1863 up to 16 December = 350 → 0 odd day(s).
Total = 3 + 0 + 0 = 3 → 3 → Wednesday.

questions.q: The absentee counts of a unit are: 47, 13, 25, 59, 47, 78, 84. Their arithmetic mean is:
questions.x: Sum = 353; number of values = 7. Mean = 353/7 = 50.43.

questions.q: At simple interest a sum doubles itself in 10 years. In how many years will it become 5 times itself at the same rate?
questions.x:
Doubling means interest = 1 × principal in 10 years, i.e. rate = 100/10 = 10% p.a.
To become 5 times, interest must be 4 × principal.
Time = (4 × 100) / 10 = 40 years. (Rule: time ∝ number of times the principal is earned as interest.)

questions.q: The average of 13 observations is 46. The average of the first 7 is 53 and that of the last 7 is 46. The 7th observation is:
questions.x:
Sum of all 13 = 13 × 46 = 598.
First 7 + last 7 = 7×53 + 7×46 = 693; the middle observation is counted twice.
Middle = 693 − 598 = 95.

questions.q: In what ratio must pulses costing ₹50 per kg be mixed with pulses costing ₹100 per kg so that the mixture is worth ₹71 per kg?
questions.x:
Alligation: (dearer − mean) : (mean − cheaper) = (100 − 71) : (71 − 50) = 29 : 21 = 29 : 21.
This is cheaper : dearer.

questions.q: The present ages of a mother and her son are in the ratio 8 : 7. 11 years ago, the ratio was 21 : 17. What is the son's present age?
questions.x:
Let ages be 8k and 7k.
(8k − 11) / (7k − 11) = 21/17 → k = 4.
Son = 7 × 4 = 28 years.

questions.q: A courier van travels from town P to town Q at 40 km/h and returns along the same road at 60 km/h. The average speed for the whole journey is:
questions.x:
For equal distances, average speed = 2uv/(u + v) (harmonic mean), not (u + v)/2.
= 2 × 40 × 60 / (40 + 60) = 4800/100 = 48 km/h.

questions.q: Arjun starts from point O and walks 8 km towards North, then turns right and walks 5 km, then turns right and walks 23 km, and finally turns right and walks 13 km. What is the shortest distance and direction of the final position from O?
questions.x:
Take O as origin, North/East positive.
North–South: +8 -23 = -15 km → 15 km South.
East–West: +5 -13 = -8 km → 8 km West.
Distance = √(8² + 15²) = 17 km, towards South-West.

questions.q:
Production of a fertiliser unit (thousand tonnes) — 2017: 100  |  2018: 125  |  2019: 120  |  2020: 130  |  2021: 115.
In which year was the percentage growth over the previous year the highest?
questions.x:
Year-on-year growth: 2018: 25%; 2019: -4%; 2020: 8.33%; 2021: -11.54%.
Highest growth: 2018 (25%). Note: the largest absolute rise need not be the largest percentage rise.

questions.q: An article is marked 60% above its cost. Two successive discounts of 20% and 10% are then given on the marked price. The resulting gain or loss per cent is:
questions.x:
Take CP = 100 → MP = 160.
After 20%: 128; after a further 10%: 115.2.
Net = 115.2 − 100 = 15.2 → 15.2% gain.
Successive discounts are multiplied, never added (20% + 10% ≠ 30%).
